bloques.titulo: Whether or not and investment questions
texto: To ask a closed question (the answer is yes or no), the conjugated verb is placed at the beginning of the sentence, immediately followed by the subject: «Kom je vandaag naar de markt?» (Do you come to the market today?). If the subject is «jij/je», remember that the verb loses the -t final in the investment («kom je?», «ga je?»).

frases.nl: Kom je vandaag naar de markt?
frases.en: You coming to the market today?

frases.nl: Ja, ik kom na mijn werk.
Is de winkel dan nog open?
frases.en: Is the store still open then?

frases.nl: Nee, hij is om zes uur gesloten.

bloques.pregunta: How does a question of yes or no be structured in Dutch?

opciones.texto: With the verb conjugated in the first absolute position
opciones.explicacion: The verb is advanced and followed by the subject («Kom je...?», «Is de winkel...?»).

opciones.texto: Placing a fixed question particle at the end of the sentence
opciones.explicacion: The Dutch does not add final particles for closed questions.

opciones.texto: Keeping exactly the same order of subject and verb of the affirmative sentence
opciones.explicacion: The direct order («Je komt...») is only affirmative, not standard question form.

bloques.frase: Kom je vandaag naar de markt?

opciones.texto: If he comes to the market today.
opciones.explicacion: «Naar de markt» is to the market and «vandaag» is today.

opciones.texto: If you can open the store tomorrow morning.
opciones.explicacion: He didn't ask you to open any shops, asked if you'd be in the market.

opciones.texto: What time does your working day end?
opciones.explicacion: This information is given by Luca as an answer, not the question raised.

bloques.pregunta: Complete to ask if trade is still open.

opciones.explicacion: She asked if it was still open («nog open»), not closed.
«Markt» is a noun (market), not an adjective state.

bloques.pregunta: What's the closing schedule according to Luca?
bloques.frase: Nee, hij is om zes uur gesloten.

opciones.explicacion: «Om zes uur gesloten» indicates that at six o'clock it is already closed.

opciones.texto: The store opens at 6: 00 in the afternoon.
Luca will be on the market at six o'clock.
opciones.explicacion: Six is the closing time of the place, not the time of its arrival.

bloques.pregunta: Complete with the particle that indicates accompanying («meekomen»).

opciones.explicacion: «Meekomen» is a separable verb; the particle «mee» goes to the end and indicates coming along with others.
«Dan» means then and does not form the separable verb.

bloques.frase: Kom je vandaag naar de markt
bloques.traduccion: You coming to the market today?
bloques.explicacion: Word conjugated in first position to form the closed question.

intro: He asks closed questions by advancing the conjugated verb to the first position.
